item.title: ASLR Exploitation Writeup
item.description: Since ASLR is active, memory addresses are not consistent I am learning about binary exploitation. This is the write-up of a challenge about bypassing binary mitigations. Initial analysis The provided program reads two inputs and prints them on stdout. Then, it continuously rereads the second input and prints both buffers on stdout. item.title: Tmux Setup
item.description: Why using tmux Tmux is a terminal multiplexer: it lets you open multiple panes, windows, and sessions seamlessly. I started using it for a neatly organized terminal setup and am perfecting its use while trying to solve CTF challenges. Being efficient in moving from one terminal window to the other is essential for ease of mind. Additionally, exploiting tmux splitting panes functions with pwntools script, I think, can give you a competitive edge when debugging exploits.

item.title: H4cked writeup
item.description: H4cked - TryHackMe Room walkthrough [H4cked]https://tryhackme.com/room/h4cked is a beginner room from TryHackMe. We’ll have to apply offensive and defensive concepts to complete the room. Oh no! We’ve been hacked! We begin by reading that some intruder has found his way into one of our machines, and the .pcapng is our forensic evidence. We can start by opening the file in Wireshark to analyze its content. item.title: About me
item.description: Hello! I am Alessandro Lo Prete. Master’s student @PoliMi. Software team member at @PoliSpace. Projects.log 6s CubeSat 12.2022-present Team Leader for the Software Subsystem (from 09.2023). Design and testing of the Flight Software for the onboard computer (Nanomind A3200). Design of mission’s mode manager. AOCS module integration. CyberChallenge 2022 Participating in CyberChallenge in 2022 allowed me to learn various topics of cybersecurity. I trained in Binary Exploitation, Reverse Engineering, Web Security, and Cryptography through CTF (Capture The Flag) challenges.
